# IntentProbe

> One local model forward. Many independently trained decisions.

IntentProbe is a research and product architecture for reading task-specific signals from the
hidden states of a small local language model. One forward pass creates a shared activation bus.
Multiple independently trained heads reuse that pass for toxicity, jailbreak, spam, sentiment,
conversation state, routing, authorization and other declared tasks. Detection, calibration, host
policy and irreversible action remain separate layers.

## Why the architecture exists

An agent workflow may ask many classification questions about the same input. Running a model or a
separate LLM-judge prompt for every question repeats substantial computation. IntentProbe keeps the
expensive model pass common while allowing each task to choose its own labelled data, layer or layer
window, token pooling, normalization, classifier, calibration and threshold. The manifest contract
is designed so compatible heads can improve independently without retraining unrelated heads.

## Measured systems result

- Backbone: exact Qwen2.5-0.5B revision, CPU, batch 1.
- Shared-path panel, 80 real held-out texts per K: one forward + 1 head averaged 68.63 ms; one
  forward + 16 heads averaged 73.34 ms. Paired mean ratio 1.069, 95% CI [1.056, 1.078].
- Separate matched ten-prompt comparator: one forward + 16 heads averaged 62.70 ms; 16 repeated
  base-model forwards averaged 956.71 ms. Repeated/shared ratio 15.26, 95% CI [15.04, 15.49].
- The repeated-forward arm omits task prompts, LM-head scoring and generation. It is a conservative
  lower bound, not a complete implementation of 16 LLM judges.
- Applying all 16 heads took 1.85 ms per input on the 80-row scaling panel. Peak RSS at K=16 was
  0.73 MiB above K=1. The 16 probe artifacts totalled 386,121 bytes.

The 16 heads form a heterogeneous research workload, not one product-quality claim. Each head keeps
its own held-out discrimination, calibration, prevalence and admission decision. The architecture
benchmark measures shared computation; task benchmarks decide whether a specific head is usable.

## Current release boundary

- Public product: the PyPI package ships the single-head Qwen2.5-0.5B tool-poisoning scanner.
- Standalone research releases: MiniCPM5-1B action-authorization probe and Qwen2.5-0.5B memory-write
  probe on Hugging Face, each with a local scorer and selection receipt.
- Measured research implementation: one-forward fan-out across 16 frozen heads, with row-level
  timing artifacts, manifests and tests committed in this repository.
- Specified next implementation: general manifest registry, hot-loading and multi-head receipt
  emission. These are not yet the public PyPI product surface.

## Research findings

- The useful readout depends on both model and task. There is no supported universal best layer or
  pooling rule. Toxicity and jailbreak labels on identical ToxicChat rows select different readouts.
- Hidden-state readouts and direct generated judgments are different interfaces. Same-backbone
  comparisons show strong task/model interaction, not universal probe superiority.
- Tool-poisoning research found strong cross-source prompt-injection generalization for the shipped
  Qwen probe, including 90.3% recall on 3,866 real HackAPrompt attacks at a clean FPR fixed to 5% on
  training data. The same-data TF-IDF baseline reached 52.8%. HackAPrompt is positive-only, so this
  is recall at a fixed clean FPR, not AUROC.
- IntentProbe does not claim to invent activation probing, layer search or shared multi-head
  inference. PIShield, TaskTracker, RouteGuard, MindGuard and related work predate or parallel parts
  of the method. The contribution is the integrated, measured architecture: task-specific readout
  manifests, a shared local activation bus, separate policy, receipts and a deployment-constrained
  readout search.

## Install the shipped scanner

```text
pip install intentprobe
intentprobe scan-config auto --format summary
```

First model-backed use downloads Qwen2.5-0.5B once. Scoring then stays local with zero telemetry.
Apache-2.0. Research preview.
